results.title: BEIJING/TAIPEI — China's military said on Tuesday it dispatched forces to monitor a U.S.
results.description:
BEIJING/TAIPEI — China's military said on Tuesday it dispatched forces to monitor a U.S. warship that entered waters around a disputed shoal in the South China Sea, while Taiwan reported an ongoing standoff with a Chinese vessel further north.

China claims almost the entire South China Sea despite overlapping claims by Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines, Taiwan, and Vietnam, with tensions running highest between Beijing and Manila.

The Chinese military's Southern Theatre Command stated that the USS Charleston entered waters adjacent to Sabina Shoal in the Spratly Islands without approval, alleging the transit jeopardized regional peace and warning Washington to cease such activities.

China's navy deployed units to track and monitor the vessel throughout the operation.

The U.S. Navy did not immediately comment, though it typically frames such movements as freedom of navigation operations.

A Philippine military spokesperson defended the mission, stating the U.S. ship did not trespass onto Chinese territory and emphasizing that no state has the legal authority to require prior permission for lawful international transit.

Friction around the feature has been severe, following an incident last month where a China Coast Guard ship rammed a Philippine vessel during a refueling mission near the shoal.

In a separate confrontation on Tuesday at the northern edge of the waterway, Taiwan's Coast Guard dispatched a patrol vessel after a Chinese Coast Guard ship breached restricted waters near the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands.

During the standoff, the Chinese vessel broadcast that the "Republic of China does not exist," prompting Taiwanese crews to respond over radio that Taiwan is a sovereign and independent nation.

Beijing's Taiwan Affairs Office did not immediately respond to inquiries, having previously warned that Taipei would bear consequences after using water cannons against a Chinese fishing boat in the area.

China has steadily intensified coast guard patrols around Taiwan, including along its eastern coastline, drawing growing concern from Western allies.

Speaking at a forum in Taipei on Tuesday, a U.S. congressional commission chair labeled China’s eastern maritime patrols highly destabilizing, while Taiwan's National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu asserted Beijing has no legal jurisdiction over those waters.

results.title: 🚨 CHINA’S ILLEGAL PRESENCE PERSISTS AT SCARBOROUGH SHOAL, BUT THE PHILIPPINES REMAINS VIGILANT.
results.description:
🚨 CHINA’S ILLEGAL PRESENCE PERSISTS AT SCARBOROUGH SHOAL, BUT THE PHILIPPINES REMAINS VIGILANT.

China speaks of peace, yet its actions at sea tell another story.

During a Philippine Coast Guard maritime domain awareness flight over Bajo de Masinloc, radio challenges involving Philippine and Chinese military aircraft and vessels were already being heard before the shoal was reached.

The mission also spotted two buoys and a floating barrier still in place, along with a Chinese research vessel, a PLA Navy warship, and a Chinese maritime militia vessel operating outside the shoal.

The Philippines continues to monitor the situation, document maritime activities, and assert its rights under international law.

Bajo de Masinloc is more than a point on the map. It represents the Philippines’ determination to protect its maritime rights against persistent pressure and intimidation.

🇵🇭 The Philippines remains watchful. Its maritime rights must be respected.

results.title: Beijing has a new rule for the South China Sea: ask permission.
results.description:
Beijing has a new rule for the South China Sea: ask permission.

On Tuesday, China's military said the USS Charleston sailed near Sabina Shoal "without approval."

Its embassy says Manila resupplied its own troops at Ayungin "without China's consent."

And the same day, near Taiwan-held Pratas, a China Coast Guard ship told Taiwan's crew the "Republic of China does not exist."

Three places, one message: you're only here if we allow it.

Here's Beijing's problem. Sabina sits about 75 nautical miles off Palawan, inside the Philippines' EEZ. Warships don't need anyone's approval to sail there. That isn't an American talking point. It's the law of the sea China itself ratified, and China's navy uses that same freedom in other countries' EEZs, including off Alaska.

Look at where the Charleston went: the shoal where a China Coast Guard ship and a Philippine vessel collided last month. Each side blames the other. The transit wasn't a request. It was an answer.

Accept "approval" once, and every patrol, every resupply, every fishing trip becomes a request. That's the real fight in the South China Sea. Not rocks. A permission slip.

results.title: Chinese Navy Shadows USS Charleston Near Contested Sabina Shoal MANILA, Philippines — USS Charleston (LCS-18) was tracked by Chinese forces
results.description:
Chinese Navy Shadows USS Charleston Near Contested Sabina Shoal

MANILA, Philippines — USS Charleston (LCS-18) was tracked by Chinese forces on Tuesday after the ship “illegally intruded” into the area surrounding a contested South China Sea maritime feature, according to Beijing. Chinese forces were dispatched to monitor the Independence-class LCS near Sabina Shoal early Tuesday, the PLA said.

Source: USNI News

results.title: ‘SEND THIS POOR VERSION OF FOREIGN GUEST, THIS HOOLIGAN BACK HOME’ Hinikayat ni Sen.
results.description:
‘SEND THIS POOR VERSION OF FOREIGN GUEST, THIS HOOLIGAN BACK HOME’

Hinikayat ni Sen. Kiko Pangilinan si Pres. Bongbong Marcos na pauwiin si Chinese Ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan sa China kasunod ng mga kontrobersiyal na pahayag ng diplomat.

Para sa senador, kung nagawa ng PBBM administration na ipakulong sina dating pangulong Rodrigo Duterte, Pastor Apollo Quiboloy, at dating House speaker Martin Romualdez, ipagbawal ang Philippine Offshore Gaming Operators (POGO), at igiit ang soberanya ng bansa laban sa Chinese aggression, kaya rin nitong pabalikin ng China si Quan.

“I have witnessed and thus know that you have what it takes, Mr President. But if you don’t use it, you lose it,” ani Pangilinan.
